messages:
emma_support: 03:17 UTC - Acme (tenant: acme-inc) reporting embedding p99 > 3.2s since ~02:50 after overnight infra changes. They included request id 01GXX7 and sample traces. Escalating for infra triage.

raj_infra: 03:25 UTC - I see nvme qdepth climb on several eu-west1 gpu hosts starting ~02:45. Kube shows a daemonset update to nvidia-driver 535.14 rolled out around 02:30 (see deploy-bot). Correlates with increased host io await.

deploy-bot: 02:31 UTC - Rollout complete: nvidia-driver 535.14 -> eu-west1-gpu (canary passed).

louis_oncall: 03:26 UTC - host-12-gpu kernel logs show repeated nvme_recovery and softirq spikes. iostat snapshot:

```
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s  await
nvme0n1         120.7   45.2  10240.0  2048.0  18.6
```

Queue depth climbs to ~300 during requests.

maya_prod: 03:28 UTC - Customer trace 01GXX7: request stalls on kv-cache miss then a disk read ~2.8s before model run. Model is small-embed-1 (fp16 q4), we pinned some shards to local disk cache for perf — looks like cache path hit disk.

raj_infra: 03:30 UTC - Repro notes: run replay load hitting /v1/embeddings for small-embed-1 with 64 concurrent clients on host-12 under current driver -> nvme qdepth spikes and latency increases. Attaching repro shell command:

```
./loadgen.sh --target https://eu-west1.redwood/embeddings --model small-embed-1 --concurrency 64 --duration 5m
```

dan_ops: 03:33 UTC - Mitigation options (short-term):
  1) Move acme traffic to eu-central pool (no driver update there).
  2) Apply temporary rate cap on embedding calls for acme.
  3) Revert driver on poisoned hosts or drain nodes.

emma_support: 03:35 UTC - Acme agreed to reroute to eu-central for 2h window; sent consent via support email.

raj_infra: 03:40 UTC - Cordoned + drained host-12; migrated pods to eu-central hosts. Initial perf improved for those pods. host-15 still showing elevated qdepth, investigating hardware-level timeouts.

louis_oncall: 03:47 UTC - Applied temporary IO tweak on host-15 (mq-deadline -> none) to test scheduler impact. Saw small drop in await and kernel softirq messages. Not a full fix.

maya_prod: 03:50 UTC - Turning on in-memory kv-pref for affected model/tenants via feature flag to avoid disk reads: FLAG_KV_PREF_IN_MEMORY=true for acme. Rolling to 10% first.

deploy-bot: 03:52 UTC - Feature flag rollout started: FLAG_KV_PREF_IN_MEMORY -> 10% eu-west1 nodes.

emma_support: 03:55 UTC - Acme reports p95 back to expected range, p99 improved to ~1.4s and acceptable for now. They're asking for root cause and timeline for full fix.

raj_infra: 04:10 UTC - Evidence points to interaction between driver 535.14 and certain NVMe firmware on a subset of hosts causing long io stalls under concurrent KV cache patterns. Filing to firmware/drivers team for bisect. CC @firmware-team.

dan_ops: 04:12 UTC - Creating follow-up incident for RCA and long-term mitigation (driver rollback plan, firmware update schedule, improved probing). For now, keep acme on eu-central until we have a patch.

maya_prod: 04:15 UTC - Added exact repro scripts and curl traces to internal playbook path (incidents/embeddings-qdepth-repro.md). Will attach iostat + dmesg snapshots.

emma_support: 04:20 UTC - I'll update customer with the mitigations and next steps. Closing this real-time triage thread; follow-up incident will track fixes.

acme-support-contact: 04:22 UTC - Thanks team — latency is acceptable for now. Please keep us posted on ETA for a permanent fix. :thumbsup:
